transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (CobaltCare Head of Security), Dr. Aaron Chen (CTO), Luis Ortega (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick security posture intake for CobaltCare Health evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Focus on SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML, RBAC model, audit logging and retention, KMS integration and key management, and data residency/retention constraints for PHI-related metadata. Agreement to run an initial pilot on Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering, pending artifact review.

Topics:
- SOC 2 and ISO documentation and timeline
- SSO/SAML and IdP integration (Okta discussed)
- RBAC, service accounts, and least privilege patterns
- Audit logs, log retention and delivery options
- Encryption at-rest/in-transit and KMS (bring-your-own-key) options
- Data retention, purging for PHI, and regional residency
- Pilot scope, benchmarks, and timeline

Action items (high level): see metadata field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm sophie, account lead on redwood, with marco our systems engineer.
[00:07] Maya: hi thanks, maya here, head of security at cobaltcare. we've got a lot to cover, so maybe start with the SOC stuff.
[00:12] Marco: sure, i'll try to map tech to the compliance asks. first question — do you have a preference for hosted vs dedicated vs private for the pilot?
[00:22] Dr. Chen: cost is a concern but so is data control. for PHI we lean private or dedicated with VPC peering. we want to understand the encryption/KMS model.
[00:30] Sophie: got it. on redwood we support hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and a private deployment model with a customer-managed control plane. for KMS you can do BYOK with cloud KMS or a dedicated HSM on private.
[00:44] Luis: quick Q — when you say BYOK, does that mean keys never leave our account? we've had issues where keys were exported in other vendors.
[00:52] Marco: good callout. with the private option the control plane is in your VPC, and customer keys stay in your KMS. with dedicated we offer VPC peering and you can bind a customer key; keys are never exported by default. i should add, i might have said "key export" weird earlier in the deck — it's not exported.
[01:08] Maya: can you point to SOC2 or ISO certs? we need Type II report, and also an SOC audit scoped for cloud SaaS with encryption and logging controls.
[01:18] Sophie: yes, we'll share the SOC2 Type II PDF and ISO summary. marco will also attach architecture notes about audit logging, where logs live, and how long they can be retained or exported.
[01:28] Speaker 2: (mumble) are there gaps on data residency?
[01:32] Dr. Chen: patient data must remain in us-east or eu-west regions, no cross-border replication unless explicitly approved.
[01:40] Marco: we support regional pinning of model serving and storage. for hosted we offer region selection; dedicated and private give more control. note: for private you can deploy on-prem if needed.
[01:50] Maya: SSO — we use Okta for SAML, SCIM for provisioning. we want RBAC aligned with SCIM groups.
[02:00] Marco: we do SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning. roles can be mapped to SCIM groups, and we have API tokens for service accounts with fine-grained scopes. one caveat: our older docs had a misspelling — folks saw "Samuel" in the logs — but it's SAML.
[02:18] Luis: how granular is RBAC? can we deny export of transcripts or limit embedding calls?
[02:25] Marco: yes — per-route role permissions. you can have a policy that allows generation but denies export or sets anonymization flags. also token-level auditing.
[02:37] Maya: speaking of audit logs, what format and delivery? do you stream to our log ingestion or is it a pull only?
[02:44] Marco: we provide both push and pull. options: push via event forwarding to your Kinesis/CloudWatch/ELK, or export S3 logs with encryption. logs include request/response metadata, token counts, latency, and anonymized content by default but can be configured to retain raw transcripts under private deployments.
[03:04] Dr. Chen: retention — we need to retain certain metadata for 7 years per compliance. do you support long-term retention and search?
[03:12] Sophie: yes, we can retain logs per customer policy. for long term we usually recommend exporting to your archival S3 and index with your SIEM. we'll outline default retention vs extended.
[03:22] Maya: if you redact PHI automatically, what's the guarantee? false positives are an ops burden.
[03:29] Marco: we have configurable PII/PHI redaction pipelines; they can run pre- or post-store. for regulated setups we push toward pre-store deterministic redaction and a human review queue for flagged items. there is some work to tune the regex/entity models — we'll include sample configs.
[03:47] Luis: on the performance side, if we go dedicated, what's the lat/throughput SLOs? we run synchronous calls in the patient flow.
[03:55] Marco: our dedicated pools have SLA-backed throughput — typical p95 latency for similar sequence lengths is 120-200ms. we can run benchmarks against your payloads; that's often part of the POC.
[04:07] Maya: any third-party pen test results? we need external validation for our board.
[04:12] Sophie: yes, we have recent pen test summaries and vuln remediation timelines. we'll share the summarized report and timing.
[04:20] Dr. Chen: what about key rotation and access? policy requires rotating keys every 90 days and restricting who can decrypt.
[04:27] Marco: for BYOK you manage rotation via your KMS; we integrate with KMS policies so decryption requires the key policy to allow the service account. audit logs show KMS decrypt calls. for host-managed keys we rotate and provide key history and attestations.
[04:42] Maya: is there a separation of duties for ops and engineers in the console? we need RBAC to prevent devs from changing retention or export rules.
[04:50] Marco: yes, console roles are separate: admin, security-audit, operator, developer, read-only. we also have an IAM integration for SSO groups. changes to retention produce an audit event and require two-person approval in high-security tiers.
[05:05] Luis: will you support token-level billing and cost attribution per team? needed to billback.
[05:11] Sophie: yes, cost attribution is available. but note, when you enable long-term retention and multiple regions cost increases. we'll show cost modeling.
[05:20] Maya: any legal requirements around subpoenas/requests? we need notification windows.
[05:26] Sophie: standard procedure: notifications per contract; for enterprise we have notification commitments unless legally prohibited. we'll surface the pattern in the contract addendum.
[05:36] Dr. Chen: can we run a pilot in our staging with masked PII? timeline: 4-week pilot, then scale if SLOs good.
[05:44] Marco: yep. typical pilot is 2-6 weeks. we do onboarding, a benchmark run, and a security checklist.
[05:50] Maya: ok last thing — any dependencies on specific cloud accounts for dedicated? we use multiple aws orgs.
[05:57] Marco: dedicated typically uses a redwood-managed cluster but peered into your VPC, or we can provision on your account for private. we'll diagram options.
[06:06] Sophie: thanks — next steps: i'll send SOC2 + ISO collateral, marco will draw the VPC and KMS flows, and maya you'll share retention policy and Okta configuration.
[06:15] Maya: yes i'll circulate that.
[06:19] Luis: fine with that, i'll help with tech details.
[06:22] Dr. Chen: let's schedule the benchmark session week of 1/26.
[06:26] Sophie: perfect. any other Qs?
[06:30] Maya: just one more — are there extra costs for BYOK or for HSM-backed keys?
[06:35] Marco: minor additional fees for HSM and private deployment licensing; we'll include cost delta in the pricing sheet.
[06:42] Sophie: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite for the benchmark.
[06:49] (call ends)
